items.title: Ceuta crisis sparks debate on expulsions and asylum
items.body: The mass arrival of 80,000 people in Ceuta on July 30 has pushed Spain toward reforming immigration law to speed up expulsions and border rejections. Ceuta and Melilla presidents demand faster expulsions and a new border protocol, while PP, Vox, and Junts also call for changes. Pedro Sánchez promised to make repatriations more efficient; a Supreme Court ruling bans hot returns of people who enter by swimming without crossing border barriers. The government built a 500-meter maritime barrier at Tarajal and another in Melilla, and a proposed reform would apply border rejection to any illegal entry point, not just fence jumps. Judges' associations reject blanket denial of asylum applications in Ceuta, insisting each case must be studied individually and that irregular entry does not remove the right to request international protection.

items.title: Valencia raises protected housing price cap to 2,568 euros
items.body: The Valencian government raised the maximum price of protected housing by 7% for 2026, setting the cap at 2,568 euros per square meter. A 70-square-meter protected home can now cost up to 179,760 euros; a 90-square-meter home up to 231,120 euros. The Valencian government cited higher material costs and reconstruction needs after the DANA. Higher protected housing prices affect affordability in the Valencian Community.

items.title: Unpaid overtime in Spain equals 68,000 full-time jobs
items.body: Spain logs 6.43 million overtime hours each week, and 2.54 million of those are neither paid nor compensated with rest, according to CCOO. That unpaid volume equals full-time employment for about 68,000 workers. Some 436,000 people perform unpaid overtime, averaging 5.8 extra hours per week. About 40% of overtime hours are unpaid and do not generate Social Security contributions, and companies have been required to register working hours since 2019.

items.title: Spain's ordinary retirement age reaches 67 in 2027
items.body: Spain's ordinary retirement age will reach 67 in 2027 for workers with fewer than 38 years and six months of contributions, completing a 15-year transition. Workers with 38 years and six months or more can retire at 65. Voluntary early retirement will be possible at 65 below that threshold or 63 above it; involuntary early retirement will start at 63 or 61. Partial retirement with a relief contract will begin at 64 below the threshold or 62 above it. The contribution period for a 100% pension base rises to 37 years in 2027.

items.title: Pensioners struggle to rent rooms as housing costs soar
items.body: Pensioners in Spain face serious difficulties finding affordable housing, including room rentals. One 70-year-old woman pays 250 euros for a room out of a 650-euro pension and shares a bathroom with two men. Economist Santiago Niño Becerra says the average person can no longer pay more. Older foreign residents living on fixed pensions may face similar strains.

items.title: Madrid collects over 100 million euros in low-emission zone fines
items.body: Madrid City Council collected more than 100 million euros in low-emission zone fines between 2022 and the first quarter of 2025, according to an audit. Total collections reached 105 million euros. Low-emission zones should be implemented in 24 municipalities with over 50,000 inhabitants, but only 10 of 19 municipalities had regulated zones by March 31, 2025; eight were fully operational. Four municipalities were drafting regulations, four were in the public information phase, and Arganda del Rey had not started. Five municipalities did not provide data: Collado Villalba, Colmenar Viejo, Getafe, Parla, and Valdemoro.

items.title: EU funds reach over one million Spanish SMEs
items.body: Spain has received over 78 billion euros, 76.5% of its allocated Next Generation EU funds. More than 1.02 million SMEs and micro-enterprises have received funding, about 68% of the total number of SMEs. Spain contributed 41% of all new EU jobs in 2025 and met 338 milestones and objectives. Brussels disbursed the sixth tranche of 6,234 million euros in August.

items.title: Monzo and Twelve prepare to launch in Spain
items.body: Neobank penetration in Spain exceeded 27% in 2025, up from 21.8% in 2024. Monzo Bank will start operations in Spain in the second half of 2026, offering 25 euros and a 2.5% interest-bearing account; Monzo has over 15 million customers. Twelve plans to launch on December 12 in Madrid, Barcelona, and Burgos. Twelve raised 1.1 million euros from Tokenized Green, Wolver Ventures, and Fundación Caja de Burgos.

items.title: DANA storm kills two in León, causes severe damage
items.body: Heavy rains from a DANA caused two deaths and severe damage in León and Castellón. Two women died in a flash flood in Manzanedo de Valdueza, León; five people were injured, including a 3-month-old baby and a 4-year-old child. Four injured people were admitted to Hospital del Bierzo in Ponferrada. The victims were in a cellar flooded by water and mud. Ponferrada's mayor declared three days of official mourning.

items.title: Riglos fire largest in Aragón's history, 17,500 hectares burned
items.body: The wildfire in Las Peñas de Riglos, Huesca, has burned 17,500 hectares, making it the largest in Aragón's history. Rain on Sunday helped contain the advance. A UME truck accident during the operation killed a young soldier. The fire can affect air quality and safety in rural areas of Aragón.
